newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Oil palm stock best Nigerian performer in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Oil palm stock best Nigerian performer in 1996.

text.p: Shares of Okomu Oil Palm Plc were the best performer in terms of price appreciation on Nigeria's stock market in 1996, a leading brokerage said on Thursday.
CSL Stockbrokers Ltd said Okomu Oil Palm yielded a 517 percent actual gain for its investors between January 1996 and end-November 1996, ahead of second-placed Unipetrol.
The brokerage house based its research on 10,000 shares bought on January 2, 1996. It also considered a 4.225 percent commission on purchase and a 3.225 percent commission on sale.

Okomu Oil Palm shares opened at 2.12 naira on January 2, 1996 and closed at 6.75 naira on November 30, 1996. During that time there was a 1:1 bonus share issue and a 15 kobo dividend, giving an actual return of 136,350 naira from an initial investment of 22,095 naira, CSL Stockbrokers said.
In the same period, 10,000 shares of Unipetrol bought at 232,630 naira on January 2 appreciated to 1,386,632 naira by end-November, an actual gain of 497 percent.
Courier company Trans-nationwide Express returned the worst performance as its fortunes tumbled by around 75 percent during the same period, the brokerage house said.
The company's shares which opened at 4.42 naira on the first day of trading last year finished at 1.07 naira by end-November.
